event.title: Two contradictory requirements
event.description: The (simulated) ministry requires registration at the one-stop shop before the hygiene certificate; the (simulated) city council requires the hygiene certificate before registration.

responses.agentName: Ministry for business creation and public administration (simulated view)
responses.message:
Here are the official texts closest to your question:

[1] Décret CFCE 2017/0877/PM, Article 2 : « L'authentification des statuts de la SARL visée à l'article 1 ci-dessus est assurée par le Chef du Centre de Formalités de Création d'Entreprises, dans un délai de vingtquatre (24) heures à compter du dépôt de la demande d'authentification. »
[2] Décret CFCE 2017/0877/PM, Visas : « REPUBLIQUE DU CAMEROUN PAIX-TRAVAIL-PATRIE DECRET N° 2 0 1 7/0 8 7 7/PM DU 2 8 FEV 2017 fixant les modalités d'authentification des Statuts de la Société à Responsabilité Limitée établis sous seing privé dans les Centres de Formalités de Création d'Entreprises au Cameroun LE PREMIER MINISTRE, CHEF DU GOUVERNEMENT, Vu… »

⚠️ Décret CFCE 2017/0877/PM : Pris en application de l'article 3(3) de la loi n° 2016/014 du 14 décembre 2016 (SARL). Texte obtenu par OCR : vérifier les montants sur le PDF officiel.

I quote them as they are. For a specific procedure (documents, fees, timelines), check with the relevant administration.

⚠️ The following texts or positions contradict each other; human review is needed before you act:
- Ministry for business creation (simulated) : « Register the business at the one-stop shop first, then apply for the hygiene certificate. » ↔ City council (simulated) : « The hygiene certificate is required before any registration. » (restaurant-opening-sequence)

responses.message:
The legal texts you provided do not contain a rule that determines the sequence between obtaining the hygiene‑security certificate (governed by the labour code) and completing the business registration (governed by the decree on authentication of SARL statutes).  

- **Article 95 of the Code du travail** sets the conditions for hygiene and safety certificates, but it does not prescribe when the certificate must be obtained relative to the company’s registration [1].  
- **Decree CFCE 2017/0877/PM** regulates the authentication of the SARL statutes and the timing of that authentication (within 24 hours after filing) [2], but it does not mention any prerequisite such as a hygiene certificate.  

Because neither text establishes a mandatory order, the contradictory requirements you describe (the ministry demanding registration first, the city council demanding the hygiene certificate first) are not resolved by the current legal framework.  

**What you can do concretely:**  

1. **Contact the two authorities** (the ministry’s one‑stop shop and the city council’s hygiene office) to obtain written clarification of their procedural requirements.  
2. **Request a joint instruction** or a “mise en demeure” from the labour inspector if the conflicting demands create an imminent risk to health and safety, as the labour code allows the inspector to order immediate measures in case of danger [1].  
3. **Proceed in parallel**: submit the SARL statutes for authentication (which must be done within 24 hours of filing) [2] while simultaneously applying for the hygiene certificate, so that whichever authority requires the document first will already have it.  

Until a specific regulation or joint administrative instruction is issued, the order remains undefined in the existing legal texts.

⚠️ The following texts or positions contradict each other; human review is needed before you act:
- Ministry for business creation (simulated) : « Register the business at the one-stop shop first, then apply for the hygiene certificate. » ↔ City council (simulated) : « The hygiene certificate is required before any registration. » (restaurant-opening-sequence)
